subject: ULP 1.12.0: cooperative AC service through BP dose/coast/park busy loops (SWR-271)
body:
Root cause of the 8h run's residual ~3/h false AC hall warnings: BP_DOSING /
BP_DOSE_COAST / BP_PARKING hold the ULP inside blocking loops for the whole
dose (~10 s), coast (5 s) and park (<=30 s) — ac_tick() never runs there, so
an AC hall pass falling inside such a window was LOST outright (a lost pass
reads as a 2x-SPR counter gap on the CPU monitor => false 'did not advance'
warning) and the AC ran open-loop on its held DAC — the owner's masking
diagnosis, confirmed in source and fixed per his 'task scheduler in the ULP
Dose/Park' direction.

ac_busy_hall_service(): ac_tick's exact hall block (level mirror, 1->0 count,
CPU wake), now shared by ac_tick and called inside every blocking BP spin
(bp_drive_window, coast, park centre-offset) — no AC revolution can be lost
to a BP busy window. ac_busy_regulate(): every-16th-window (~0.8 s), 150 ms-
capped, 8-interval AC Simple-P slice between BP drive windows in DOSING and
PARKING; its combined poll keeps counting BP encoder edges into the caller's
ledger so dose/park tick accounting stays EXACT; dose-tail guard (160 edges)
keeps target-crossing out of any slice; the park slice watches the BP hall so
home is never overshot; no kick/ladder/stall-recovery coupling. ac_busy_slices
telemetry proves regulation ran.

Gates: canary linked, no libgcc, op headroom 696 B (was 1296; LOW accepted —
max call depth unchanged vs the existing regulate_pump->run_simple_p chain,
.stack_canary + firmware per-tick check armed, 184 B above the 512 fail
line). Registry 1.64: SWR-271 + 5 structure tests; 138 reqs, 120 PASS, 0
FAIL. Deploy pending board-on-USB.

body:

RTC slow memory is random noise; the ULP start's liveness gate
(INITIALIZED != 0) was satisfied by that noise and a session resumed
onto a NEVER-EXECUTED ULP: no regulation, parks never serviced, encoder
counts frozen (valve/tape moves gated on them misbehaved), DAC latched

board's own address map and that a manual reload came straight up
(v1.9.0, canary clear, INITIALIZED advancing).

requires it to ADVANCE (>= 2), one reload retry, then a hard failure;

advancing) BEFORE any pump is enabled — on failure the session is NOT
resumed and the device falls back to AWAIT_CALIBRATION with an error
naming the required power-cycle.

entry+60 s while the BP fought its dead-point start.

subject: ULP 1.3.3 / fw 0.1.73: adaptive self-tuning motor kick-start (SWR-126)
body:
Every operational motor-start site now routes through ONE try_kick_start helper
that learns the working start power per session — directly targeting the BP
dose-completion failures (collect/prepare timeout -> fatal reset).

Algorithm (uniform at every start site): drive at the pump's learned start
register; wait <=50 ms for the first encoder edge (sample_encoder's first-edge
window). Edge -> started, keep the power. No edge -> set MOTOR_START_FAIL + wake
CPU (logged), stop the motor, escalate start power +200 (register -= 200, MORE
power, clamped to full DAC_MAX_POWER), persist the new register in the shared var,
retry next tick. One attempt per tick + clamped register => no infinite loop. The
escalated value persists for the session and resets to the board_config default
at boot — so it ideally escalates only once per session.

Start sites unified (esp32/pump_regulator/main/ulp/main.c): regulate_pump spin-up
(AC + BP running) + mid-run stall recovery; bp_enter_dosing / bp_enter_parking via
bp_dose_park_kick; BP_DOSING + BP_PARKING mid-stall (replaced the one-shot
nudge-to-DAC_START). New per-pump shared vars ac_dac_start / bp_dac_start.

Config: board_config DAC_START_AC = 700 power (reg 3395), DAC_START_BP = 3200
power (reg 895, strong stiction-breaking) — both overlay-tunable; firmware
converts power->register (4095 - power) at ULP init and logs "BP/AC start power
raised to <pwr> (kick reg=<reg>)" on each escalation.
